title: Part (II): the Lipschitz push-forward commutes with the boundary, from the reference sequences and Part (I) (supplied Step 7)
statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; D_q(ℝ^p) := GeometricCurrentOn univ q and D^q(ℝ^p) := TestFormOn univ q; M = mass, spt = support, ∂ = boundary; for a test form φ, dφ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ q φ, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative φ; |γ| := covectorEuclideanNorm γ; A_ρ := thickening ρ A; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞); a map g is proper on F if g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K. For g : ℝ^p → ℝ^q, ω ∈ D^j(ℝ^q), η ∈ D^j(ℝ^p) and A ⊆ ℝ^p, 'η is compatible with (g, ω) near A' means: there is an open N ⊇ A with η(x) = ω(g(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ g x) for all x ∈ N. For X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m), G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} and S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}), LipPF(X, G, S) means: for every sequence (G_n) of C^∞ maps ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, every open O ⊇ spt X and every L ∈ ℝ such that eventually ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ L for all x ∈ O, and G_n → G uniformly on O, and for every ω ∈ D^k(ℝ^{m′}) and every sequence (η_n) in D^k(ℝ^m) such that eventually η_n is compatible with (G_n, ω) near spt X, the sequence X(η_n) converges to S(ω). Assume (RS): for all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r ∈ ℝ and F ⊆ ℝ^m such that r > 0, F is closed, G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and G is proper on F, there are C^∞ maps G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2}, and G_n proper on F for all sufficiently large n (this is the conclusion of the sibling reference_sequence); and assume the following statement (I) (Part (I) of the selected parent, proved by the sibling existence): (I) For all m, m′, k ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_k(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ such that M(∂Y) < ∞ for every j ∈ ℕ and Y ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with k = j + 1 and HEq Y X, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0 and r > 0 such that G is Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X) and G⁻¹(K) ∩ spt X is compact for every compact K: there is S ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S) such that every S′ ∈ D_k(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S′) equals S, M(S) ≤ Λ^k·M(X) (in ℝ≥0∞) and spt S ⊆ closure(G(spt X)). Then the following holds: (II) For all m, m′, j ∈ ℕ, X ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^m) with M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞, G, Λ, r as in (I) (Λ-Lipschitz on thickening r (spt X), proper on spt X) and S ∈ D_{j+1}(ℝ^{m′}) with LipPF(X, G, S): LipPF(∂X, G, ∂S).
